theorems.title: Resolution-Handoff Continuity Theorem — fixed Bandwidth
theorems.statement: If Resolution handoff commutes, presentations share retained Formal Identity, the Identity Witness remains valid, and merged essential distinctions remain recoverable through provenance, then non-injective coarsening is structurally continuous under the declared contract.
assumptions: rho_Ri = q_ji o rho_Rj
same retained formal object
valid Identity Witness
merged essential distinctions recoverable
theorems.conclusion: coarsening may change distinguishability without erasing canonical structure

theorems.title: Bandwidth Modifier Resolution-Descent Condition
theorems.statement: A typed Bandwidth modifier M descends to a well-defined Resolution readout map only if source Resolution equivalence is respected by the target readout: a~_R b implies M(a)~_R' M(b).
assumptions: typed Bandwidth modifier
declared source/target Resolution equivalences
theorems.conclusion: induced readout map exists iff equivalence is respected

theorems.title: Recovery Witness Fiber-Separation Theorem
theorems.statement: Let F_c be the fine-lineage fiber over one coarse Resolution handoff/readout c, and let W be the retained recovery-witness map on F_c. A witness-mediated recovery selector returns a unique declared fine lineage for every element of F_c if and only if W separates distinct recovery-relevant lineages on F_c (equivalently: W restricted to F_c has no collisions under the declared structural equivalence).
assumptions: non-injective handoff fiber F_c is declared
recovery equivalence is declared
selector may use only retained witness data and may not invent suppressed structure
theorems.conclusion: Unique lineage recovery is equivalent to fiber separation by the retained witness; non-separating witness bundles are insufficient without an additional discriminator.

theorems.title: Recovery Context Quotient Theorem
theorems.statement: Let H be the admitted typed History path algebra and let T_rec be the declared recovery-test family. Define h ~_Rec k when all tests in T_rec agree after every admissible left/right History context in which both histories can be compared. Then ~_Rec is a compositional congruence; Sig_Rec(h)=[h]_Rec has well-defined induced composition; the quotient is recovery-sufficient for T_rec; and among compositional signatures preserving all T_rec distinctions it is the coarsest (least structurally discriminating) such signature.
assumptions: History paths compose associatively on their admitted typed sector
recovery test family is explicitly declared for the selected recovery contract
tests are compared only in contexts where both composites are typed/admissible
signature sufficiency is relative to the declared test family; no claim of finite representation is assumed
theorems.conclusion: Full ordered History need not be retained as the visible recovery signature in principle; the abstract minimal compositional signature is the Recovery Context Equivalence class, while full History/provenance remains recoverable upstream under the continuity contract.

theorems.title: Recovery Signature Realization Theorem
theorems.statement: Let Sig_Rec=H/~_Rec be the closed abstract recovery signature quotient and let sigma:H->S be a concrete signature compatible with History composition. Then sigma is an exact realization of the minimal recovery signature iff ker(sigma)=~_Rec. If ker(sigma) strictly contains ~_Rec, sigma is recovery-insufficient; if ker(sigma) is strictly contained in ~_Rec, sigma over-resolves the declared recovery structure; if neither inclusion holds, both defect types occur.
assumptions: Recovery Context Quotient Theorem is closed
concrete signature sigma is typed on the compared History sector
signature equality/equivalence is declared
composition compatibility is tested separately
theorems.conclusion: Concrete signature realization becomes a kernel-equality problem; D57/Sig_Hol cannot be promoted as minimal until this equality and composition are established.

theorems.title: Signature Envelope Normalization Theorem
theorems.statement: Let h be a typed History path h:x->y. Let scope be the declared comparison/classifier scope for the signature and let provenance be recoverably bound to the signature QMO address. Then the flat record Sig_Hol(h)=(src,tgt,[h],Hol_Conn,Hol_chi,Hol_Id,scope,provenance) is recoverably equivalent, as a complete API record, to the typed normal form <x,y;scope,provenance | [h],Hol_Conn,Hol_chi,Hol_Id>. This factoring relocates information between type/envelope and payload but does not alter the signature kernel when equality compares the complete joined record.
assumptions: History source and target are typed functions on h
scope remains explicitly declared and recoverable
QMO metadata/provenance lookup is one-to-one and append-only for the signature address
comparison uses the complete joined record rather than payload alone
theorems.conclusion: src,tgt,scope,provenance need not be treated as homogeneous payload fields in field-redundancy search. No structural payload field is thereby proven redundant.

theorems.title: Signature Role Separation Theorem
theorems.statement: Let Sig_Rec be defined as the coarsest compositional signature preserving the declared recovery tests. Let Sig_Hol be the source D57 typed signature that packages, without identifying, connection, chirality, Identity, History, scope, and provenance effects. Then exact kernel equality ker(Sig_Hol)=~_Rec is not a source requirement for Sig_Hol. It becomes a requirement only under the additional implementation contract that Sig_Hol is intended to realize the minimal recovery-selector role. Otherwise Sig_Hol may intentionally retain diagnostically useful distinctions beyond recovery minimality.
assumptions: Recovery Context Quotient Theorem is closed
D57 source signature is interpreted according to FORMAL/06_HOLONOMY.md
no extra source claim identifies the diagnostic role with minimal recovery realization
theorems.conclusion: Holonomy field-redundancy/minimality is an optional implementation optimization, not a foundational blocker for the recovery architecture or the number program.

theorems.title: Object-Before-Scalarization Theorem
theorems.statement: Within the mounted Bandwidth Algebra, the formal object A_B and its Resolution readout are defined independently of any scalar valuation. BA-D11 introduces beta only when a scalar summary is needed and explicitly states that the result is a readout rather than the definition of Bandwidth. Hence scalar/numerical description is downstream of at least one fully defined native mathematical object.
assumptions: Mounted Bandwidth Algebra v1.0 definitions are admitted
Scalar valuation is interpreted according to BA-D11/BA-D12
No claim is made that every numerical object arises this way
theorems.conclusion: A formal mathematical object need not be numerical in order to exist or be manipulated; numerical/scalar summary can be a later readout role.

theorems.title: Unit Value Is Not Counting Theorem
theorems.statement: Let U_1 contain admissible Unit-String configurations with ell(c)=1 for every c in U_1, and let A_B(U_1) admit reconfiguration moves between distinct configurations. Then the token 1 in ell(c)=1 is invariant across a family containing potentially multiple distinct configurations. Therefore its structural role in this source construction is normalization, not enumeration of how many configurations exist.
assumptions: Unit String source definition ell(c)=1 is admitted
Distinct admissible configurations/reconfiguration moves are permitted in A_B(U_1)
No identification of the glyph 1 with conventional arithmetic ontology is assumed
theorems.conclusion: A 1-labeled valuation can have a non-counting structural role; numeral glyph alone does not determine number ontology.

theorems.title: Valuation-Fiber Factorization Theorem
theorems.statement: For any declared function v:X->V, define x~_v y iff v(x)=v(y). Then ~_v is an equivalence relation, the quotient projection pi_v:X->Q_v=X/~_v is well-defined, and v factors uniquely through its image by v_bar([x])=v(x). The induced v_bar is injective onto im(v).
assumptions: v is a function
equality on V is an equivalence relation
theorems.conclusion: Valuation outputs correspond to valuation-fiber classes; this factorization uses no arithmetic structure on V.

theorems.title: Fiber Structure Is Not Numericality Theorem
theorems.statement: The fiber-equivalence and quotient-factorization construction applies to every function/readout, including qualitative classifier readouts. Therefore being a quotient label of source-object fibers is a generic readout property and is insufficient to characterize numericality.
assumptions: @theorem_valuation_factorization
@classifier_readout_role is admitted as a non-numerical/generic classification role
theorems.conclusion: Numerical role requires structure beyond functional fiber partition and quotient labeling.

theorems.title: Order Precedes Scalarization Theorem
theorems.statement: Bandwidth Algebra BA-D10 defines B1<=B2 by structural inclusion of available transformations, while BA-D11 introduces scalar beta only when a scalar summary is needed. Hence the native order is meaningful before scalar numerical valuation is introduced.
assumptions: Bandwidth Algebra BA-D10
Bandwidth Algebra BA-D11
theorems.conclusion: Order/comparison alone cannot be the missing condition that makes a valuation output numerical.

theorems.title: Unit-Order Underdetermination Theorem
theorems.statement: Let a valuation-output domain V carry only its valuation-fiber equality, an order <=_V, and distinguished unit u. For every automorphism phi of this declared structure with phi(u)=u, v and phi∘v satisfy the same named fiber/order/unit contract. Therefore, whenever a nonidentity such phi exists, that contract underdetermines the readout coordinate and supplies no unique quantitative or arithmetic semantics.
assumptions: V has declared equality/order/unit only
phi preserves the declared structure and fixes u
theorems.conclusion: Unit plus order can constrain a value domain without closing numerical role; extra scale/transport structure is required whenever the stabilizer is nontrivial.
